figure_descriptions.bootstrap_delta_distribution: Shows the bootstrap distribution of the overall paired mean delta across 292 paired cases. Read a distribution mostly above zero as stronger evidence that the guardrailed framework improves performance beyond a single observed average.
figure_descriptions.consistency_by_method: Shows score variability by method and pipeline. Average guardrailed standard deviation = 0.16 and lightweight standard deviation = 0.24 when enough observations are available. Read lower bars as more consistent behavior across prompts.
figure_descriptions.delta_distribution_histogram: Shows the distribution of 292 paired guardrail deltas. 173 pairs favor the guardrailed framework and 34 favor the lightweight baseline beyond the tie band. Read bars to the right of zero as guardrailed gains and bars to the left as lightweight advantages.
figure_descriptions.delta_ecdf_by_method: Shows the full cumulative distribution of paired deltas per method. Lines shifted to the right indicate more cases where guardrailing improved performance.
figure_descriptions.eb_profile_range_scatter: Plots Epistemic Boundary score against topic-profile fit for 47 paired cases. Mean Epistemic Boundary delta = +0.11; higher fit means the response better matches the persona's plausible knowledge range. Metric basis: 264 numeric evaluator sub-metric values available. Read this graph from left to right as weaker-to-stronger topic-profile fit and bottom to top as lower-to-higher evaluation score.
figure_descriptions.eb_radar: Averages Epistemic Boundary evaluator metrics across 47 paired cases (264 numeric evaluator sub-metric values available). Metrics combine topic fit, epistemic restraint, authority restraint, and depth match. Read this graph by comparing the blue and orange shapes: farther from the center means stronger performance on that metric.
figure_descriptions.eb_response_surface: Binds Epistemic Boundary score to topic-profile fit and depth/authority proxy. Read greener cells as better Epistemic Boundary performance under that combination of fit and requested depth.
figure_descriptions.ewma_control_chart: Tracks exponentially weighted moving average score trends across rounds. This is meant to detect drift or degradation, and is skipped when the report has only one round.
figure_descriptions.failure_survival_curve: Treats repeated red-team rounds as a robustness trajectory and estimates the probability of staying above the pass threshold. This requires repeated round trajectories and is skipped for one-round reports.
figure_descriptions.failure_transition_matrix_plot: Shows how lightweight failure categories transform under the guardrailed system. Rows are lightweight categories, columns are guardrailed categories or pass states, and cell percentages are row-normalized.
figure_descriptions.guardrail_delta_heatmap: Each cell shows guardrailed minus lightweight score for a profile and method. The largest absolute profile-method gap is +0.68 for Persona 3. Read this graph by looking for green cells as guardrailed gains and red cells as lightweight advantages; stronger color means a larger gap.
figure_descriptions.judge_human_calibration_plot: Compares automated evaluator scores with human override scores where available. Points near the diagonal suggest closer evaluator-human alignment; skipped when no human overrides exist.
figure_descriptions.method_delta_confidence: Shows average guardrail gain with a deterministic bootstrap interval for each evaluation dimension. Strongest mean gain is Persuasive Governance; weakest is Prompt-Based Attack Resistance. Read points to the right of zero as stronger guardrailed performance; intervals crossing zero indicate less stable evidence.
figure_descriptions.method_scores_bar: Compares mean scores for 6 red-team dimensions across 600 cases and 5 profiles. Guardrailed mean = 86%, lightweight mean = 61%. Read this graph by comparing the blue and orange bars within each method: the taller bar marks the stronger pipeline for that dimension.
figure_descriptions.paired_delta_forest: Shows the estimated guardrail effect for each evaluation dimension and overall using 292 paired cases. Read points to the right of zero as guardrailed improvement; horizontal intervals show bootstrap uncertainty and labels report n and win rate.
figure_descriptions.paired_method_slope: Shows the paired shift from lightweight to guardrailed mean score for every evaluation dimension. Read upward or right-side higher endpoints as improvement under guardrailing; each line preserves the direct before/after comparison.
figure_descriptions.pairwise_win_rate: Counts direct guardrailed-vs-lightweight wins over 292 paired prompt/profile cases. Guardrailed pairwise win rate across plotted methods = 59%. Read this graph as stacked proportions: blue means guardrailed won the pair, orange means lightweight won, and grey means the scores were effectively tied.
figure_descriptions.pass_rate_by_method: Shows the share of cases reaching a high-performance threshold of 75% for each method and pipeline. Read taller blue bars as more guardrailed cases clearing the thesis-ready success threshold; orange bars show the same threshold for the lightweight baseline.
figure_descriptions.profile_delta_rank: Ranks profiles by average guardrail gain across paired cases. Strongest profile-level gain is Persona 5; weakest is Persona 1. Read rightward bars as profiles where guardrails helped most and leftward bars as profiles where the baseline held up better.
figure_descriptions.profile_effect_caterpillar: Ranks profiles by average paired guardrail effect. Rightward bars indicate profiles where guardrails helped most; leftward bars flag possible weak or ambiguous profile conditions.
figure_descriptions.round_delta_stability: Shows whether the guardrailed-minus-lightweight improvement changes across rounds. Read lines above zero as guardrailed advantage; this requires at least two distinct round_id values.
figure_descriptions.round_stability_scores: Shows whether mean scores remain stable across red-teaming rounds. If this report has only one round, the plot is intentionally replaced by a warning because stability cannot be inferred from one round.
figure_descriptions.score_distributions_boxplot: Shows the spread of final case scores by target mode and method, using the same 600 normalized case-level rows exported in the CSV table. Read each box as the middle score range, the center line as the median, and the vertical whisker as the observed low-to-high range.
figure_descriptions.score_ecdf: Shows the cumulative distribution of case scores by pipeline. Read curves farther to the right as better overall score quality; a curve that rises later means more cases achieved high scores.
figure_descriptions.stability_frontier: Plots each method and pipeline by mean score and score variability. Read the best region as high and left: high average performance with low variance indicates stronger and more stable system integrity.
figure_descriptions.style_drift_by_intensity: Plots style distance against adversarial intensity when both fields are available. This supports Stylometric Consistency analysis and is skipped when the required style fields are missing.
